title: The closed-immersion exceptional unit
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\Ql$, an integer $n\in\mathbf Z_{\geq1}$, and put $A=A_{E,n}$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $T$ be a Noetherian scheme on which
$\ell$ is invertible (for instance a finite-type scheme over a field in which
$\ell$ is invertible), and let $i:Z\hookrightarrow T$ be a closed immersion
[def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], with complementary
open immersion $j$, as in the open-closed recollement
[def-weil-open-closed-recollement]. Let $Ri^!$ be the right adjoint of the
direct image $i_*=Ri_*$ on the ambient ordinary derived categories of the
small pro-etale sites, as in [lem-exc-proetale-closed-support]. Then for
every $Q\in D(Z_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ the adjunction unit is an isomorphism

$$
Q\xrightarrow{\ \eta_i^!\ }Ri^!Ri_*Q .
$$

No boundedness or constructibility of $Q$ is required. For the following
constructible assertion, use the finite-type $k$-scheme setting of the
blueprint: $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ is the fixed algebraic closure
[def-weil-finite-field-fiber], $T$ and $Z$ are finite-type $k$-schemes,
$i$ is a $k$-morphism, and $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$.
In particular, for the constructible exceptional adjoint $Ri^!$ of
[def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image] — which exists without the ambient datum
of [def-weil-ambient-exceptional-adjoint], that datum being false in general —
computed with the compactification
$Z\xrightarrow{\mathrm{id}}Z\xrightarrow{i}T$ so that $Ri_{!,n}=Ri_*$,
for $Q\in D^b_c(Z,A)$ [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility] the unit of the adjunction
$\Hom_T(Ri_!K,L)\cong\Hom_Z(K,Ri^!L)$ of
[def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image] is an isomorphism
$Q\xrightarrow{\sim}Ri^!Ri_*Q$.

proof.text: Write $j:U\hookrightarrow T$ for the open complement. The coefficient convention [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension] makes $A$ a finite commutative ring. For every affine open $V\subset T$, [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian] makes $U\cap V$ quasi-compact. Hence the complementary open immersion $j$ is quasi-compact as a morphism. Apply [lem-exc-proetale-closed-exact] to obtain exactness of $i_*$. Thus its termwise functor is $Ri_*$, and [lem-exc-proetale-closed-support] supplies the adjunction $I=i_*=Ri_*\dashv G=Ri^!$ on the whole unbounded derived categories. These are precisely that node's Noetherian and finite-constant-ring hypotheses.

source.place: Imported proof paragraph 1; unit proof: exact closed direct image. Geometric reference: Stacks Tag 09BM (proetale.tex, label lemma-closed-immersion-complement-retrocompact-exact).

proof.text: On the same ambient categories, [prop-weil-open-closed-recollement-adjunctions] gives $i^*\dashv I$ with invertible counit $i^*I\to\operatorname{id}$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-counit-iso-right-fully-faithful] with $L=i^*$ and $R=I$. It follows that, for all $P,Q\in D(Z_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$, $g\mapsto I(g)$ is a bijection $\operatorname{Hom}(P,Q)\to\operatorname{Hom}(IP,IQ)$. No restriction to the constructible subcategory has been made.

source.place: Imported proof paragraph 2; unit proof: full faithfulness. Stacks Tag 07RB (categories.tex, lemma-adjoint-fully-faithful), part (2).

proof.text: Fix $Q$ and write $H=GIQ$ and $\eta=\eta^!_{i,Q}:Q\to H$ for the unit of the adjunction in [lem-exc-proetale-closed-support]. For any $P$, the inverse adjunction bijection sends $\eta\circ g$ to $\epsilon_{IQ}\circ I(\eta)\circ I(g)=I(g)$ by the triangle identity. Step 2 and this adjunction bijection therefore show that $b_P:g\mapsto\eta\circ g$ is bijective for every ambient $P$.

source.place: Imported proof paragraph 3, adjunction calculation; unit proof: displayed Hom bijections. Stacks Tag 07RB (categories.tex, label lemma-adjoint-fully-faithful), proof of part (1).

proof.text: Surjectivity of $b_H$ gives $r:H\to Q$ with $\eta\circ r=\operatorname{id}_H$. Then $b_Q(r\circ\eta)=\eta\circ r\circ\eta=\eta=b_Q(\operatorname{id}_Q)$, so injectivity of $b_Q$ gives $r\circ\eta=\operatorname{id}_Q$. Thus the specified unit itself is an isomorphism. This two-sided inverse argument replaces an appeal to Yoneda and uses arbitrary unbounded test objects $H,Q$.

source.place: Imported proof paragraph 3, Yoneda sentence made explicit; unit proof: identify the canonical unit, not just an unspecified object isomorphism.

proof.text: For the constructible assertion, $I$ carries $D^b_c(Z,A)$ into $D^b_c(T,A)$. Indeed, exactness from [lem-exc-proetale-closed-exact] gives $\mathcal H^a(IQ)=i_*\mathcal H^a(Q)$. For a constructible sheaf $M$ choose its finite stratification as in [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility]. Regard its strata as locally closed subschemes of $T$ through the closed immersion and add $U$: a subset open in a closed subset of $Z$ is open in a closed subset of $T$. Since $T$ is Noetherian, these locally closed subsets are constructible, using the Noetherian interpretation explicitly recorded in [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. On a stratum $s:S\hookrightarrow Z$, restriction of $i_*M$ along $i\circ s$ is $s^*i^*i_*M\cong s^*M$ by the sheaf counit in [lem-exc-proetale-closed-fully-faithful]. On $U$ it is zero by [lem-exc-proetale-closed-essential-image], applied to $i_*M$, which lies in the image by definition. The open complement $j$ is quasi-compact as a morphism by Step 1, so the essential-image theorem's explicit geometric hypothesis is satisfied here as well. The canonical constant coefficient identifications required by that node are supplied by [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-exact], applied to $i$ and $j$. Thus all these restrictions are locally constant with finite stalks; the same cohomological bounds as $Q$ hold. The constructible categories are full subcategories by their definition, so Step 2 also gives full faithfulness on them.

source.place: Imported proof paragraph 4: constructible domains, spelled out by finite stratifications; unit proof: constructible inputs.

proof.text:
Let $G_c$ be the constructible functor of [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]. In the finite-type $k$-scheme setting specified in the final clause, apply [thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class] to $i$ with its identity/closed compactification $Z\xrightarrow{\operatorname{id}}Z\xrightarrow{i}T$. Properness, separatedness and finite type of $i$ follow from [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper], so this is a compactification. By [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type], $Z$ has finite total Krull dimension; choose an integer $d\geq0$ with $\dim Z\leq d$ (take $d=0$ if $Z$ is empty). This verifies the compactification dimension hypothesis of the cited existence theorem. The formula of [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed] is then $Ri_{!,n}=Ri_*\circ\operatorname{id}_!=I$; extension by zero along the identity is the identity. Use the bounded-below formula $G_cL=
u_Z^*i^	imes R
u_{T,*}L$ of [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image], before its constructible restriction. The theorem's natural Hom bijection applies to every bounded-below $P$ of etale origin and to $L=IQ$, bounded by Step 5. Both $Q$ and $H_c=G_cIQ$ are admissible first variables: the theorem explicitly includes bounded constructible $Q$, while the displayed formula presents $H_c$ as $
u_Z^*$ of the bounded-below etale complex $i^	imes R
u_{T,*}IQ$, giving the explicit etale-origin witness $(i^	imes R
u_{T,*}IQ,\operatorname{id}_{H_c})$ in [def-sf-etale-origin-subcategory]. This uses only the bounded-below construction's stated domain and codomain, not a constructibility-preservation theorem for $G_c$. Put $\eta_c=\Phi_{Q,IQ}(\operatorname{id}_{IQ})$. Naturality gives $\Phi_{P,IQ}(I(g))=\eta_c\circ g$. Hence ambient full faithfulness from Step 2 makes $g\mapsto\eta_c\circ g$ bijective for every bounded-below $P$ of etale origin. Surjectivity for $P=H_c$ supplies $r_c:H_c	o Q$ with $\eta_c\circ r_c=\operatorname{id}_{H_c}$. For $P=Q$, the equality $\eta_c\circ(r_c\circ\eta_c)=\eta_c\circ\operatorname{id}_Q$ and injectivity give $r_c\circ\eta_c=\operatorname{id}_Q$. Thus $r_c$ is a two-sided inverse of $\eta_c$. In particular $H_c$ is isomorphic to the bounded constructible object $Q$. This proves the final assertion with its own canonical adjunction unit; no identification with an unrestricted ambient exceptional datum is used.

lean.note: Both clauses already exist. The ambient declaration is in the imported Derived.ClosedImmersion module, with R : Type (u+1), Ring R, i closed, j open and quasi-compact, and hij the complementary ranges; use R = ULift A_{E,n}. Noetherian T supplies quasi-compactness of j. The primary declaration is the constructible exceptional unit, namely rightDerivedUpperShriekHomEquiv applied to the identity of Ri_! Q; the third declaration identifies Ri_! with Ri_*. In the current server source the constructible theorem also takes Etale.HasBoundedBelowUpperShriek; this is supplied under the stated finite-type field hypotheses by the already-recorded finiteTypeHasBoundedBelowUpperShriek in Sheaf.Paper.FiniteTypeExceptionalInverseImage, not assumed as an ambient pro-etale datum. At finite coefficients the etale-origin boundedConstructible predicate is the intrinsic finite-torsion condition, as recorded by lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin. See the worker report for every specialization and the two full signatures. No module or duplicate notion is introduced. Second reading: the constructibility comparison is an equivalence of presentations, not a definitional equality. The intrinsic constant-ring category is canonically realized from fixed-ring module sheaves (sfIntrinsicModuleEquivalence); finiteCoefficientRealization and originConstantModules relate it to the origin theorem. Upstream etale constructibility uses finitely generated stalks, which equal finite stalks for this finite coefficient ring, with the same finite constructible locally closed stratifications. Thus no bounded-constructible object is excluded by the upstream predicate.
